Description: explicit — validate style JSON with CLI tool after migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and want to check whether my exported style JSON is compatible before deploying. Is there a CLI tool I can run on the file?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a quick-start guide to **validate a Mapbox-style JSON file for MapLibre-GL** before you ship it.  
The official CLI is shipped with the **`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec`** package and is called **`gl-style-validate`**.

---

## 1️⃣ Install the validator (once)

```bash
# If you already have a project with a package.json
npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec

# Or install it globally (optional)
npm i -g @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec
```

> **Why the `-D` flag?**  
> The validator is a development-time tool only; it isn’t needed at runtime.

---

## 2️⃣ Run the CLI

```bash
# From the project root (or any folder that can see the file)
npx gl-style-validate path/to/style.json
```

If you installed the package globally you can also run:

```bash
gl-style-validate path/to/style.json
```

### Typical output

```
✔ style.json – valid MapLibre style (0 errors, 3 warnings)

Warnings:
  1️⃣  source "mapbox" – unknown source type "vector". Did you mean "vector" from a non-Mapbox URL?
  2️⃣  layer "water" – property "paint['fill-color']" uses a Mapbox-only expression "interpolate".
  3️⃣  sprite URL is a relative path; make sure it resolves from the style location.
```

* `✔` → the file **passes** validation (no fatal errors).  
* `⚠` → warnings – the style will still load, but you may want to clean them up.  
* `✖` → errors – the map will **fail to load** until they’re fixed.

---

## 3️⃣ What the validator checks

| Category | What it looks for | MapLibre-specific notes |
|----------|-------------------|--------------------------|
| **JSON schema** | Correct JSON syntax, required top-level keys (`version`, `sources`, `layers`, …) | Uses the **MapLibre Style Specification** (v8-compatible). |
| **Source definitions** | Valid `type` (`vector`, `raster`, `geojson`, `image`, `canvas`) and URL format | MapLibre **does not understand** `mapbox://` URLs. The validator will flag any `mapbox://` source as an error. |
| **Layer references** | `source` and `source-layer` exist, correct case-sensitivity | If you renamed a source after exporting from Mapbox Studio, you must update the style JSON accordingly. |
| **Sprite & glyph URLs** | Must be reachable HTTP(S) URLs or relative paths that resolve from the style location | MapLibre does **not** fetch sprites from `mapbox://sprites/…`. |
| **Expressions & functions** | Only expressions supported by the MapLibre spec are allowed | Mapbox-only functions (e.g., `["heatmap-color", …]` before v8) will be reported as errors. |
| **Deprecated properties** | Flags usage of `layout.visibility` set to `"none"` on layers that are hidden by a filter, etc. | Warnings only – MapLibre still renders them but they may be removed in future releases. |
| **Version compatibility** | `version` must be `8` (or `7` for legacy) and match the spec version you’re targeting | MapLibre v6+ expects style spec v8; older versions may accept v7. |

---

## 4️⃣ Using the validator in CI / npm scripts

Add a script to your `package.json`:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "style:lint": "gl-style-validate src/style.json"
  }
}
```

Then run it locally:

```bash
npm run style:lint
```

Or in a CI pipeline (GitHub Actions example):

```yaml
name: Style validation
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  validate-style:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run style:lint
```

If the command exits with a non-zero status (i.e., any **error**), the CI job fails, preventing a broken style from being merged.

---

## 5️⃣ Common “error → fix” patterns

| Error message | Why it happens | Quick fix |
|---------------|----------------|-----------|
| **`source "my-source" – unknown source type "vector"`** | The source URL is still a `mapbox://` URL or the `type` is misspelled. | Replace `url: "mapbox://…"` with a proper HTTP(S) URL (e.g., `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/…`) and ensure `type: "vector"`. |
| **`layer "road-label" – unknown source-layer "road_label"`** | The `source-layer` name in the style does not exist in the new vector tileset. | Open the tileset’s `metadata.json` (or use `mapbox-gl-js`/`maplibre-gl-js` `querySourceFeatures`) to get the correct layer name, then edit the style JSON. |
| **`paint['fill-color'] uses a Mapbox-only expression "interpolate"`** | The expression syntax is fine, but the **input type** (e.g., `["zoom"]`) is not allowed in MapLibre v5+ without the `["interpolate"]` wrapper. | Rewrite the expression using MapLibre-compatible syntax, e.g., `["interpolate", ["linear"], ["zoom"], 5, "#f8f4f0", 10, "#e0e0e0"]`. |
| **`sprite URL is a relative path; make sure it resolves from the style location`** | Relative sprite URLs work only if the style file is served from the same directory. | Either host the sprite folder next to the style file or change the URL to an absolute path (`https://my.cdn.com/sprites/sprite`). |
| **`glyphs URL is missing`** | MapLibre needs a glyphs endpoint for text rendering. | Add `"glyphs": "https://fonts.openfreemap.org/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf"` (or any compatible glyph service). |

---

## 6️⃣ When you need a **more visual** check

* **Maputnik** – a web-based style editor that loads a JSON file, validates it, and highlights problems in the UI.  
  ```bash
  npx maputnik --style path/to/style.json
  ```
* **MapLibre GL JS “debug mode”** – add `hash: true, preserveDrawingBuffer: true` and open the browser console; any style-loading errors will appear as `Error: Style validation failed …`.

Both are great for quick iteration, but the **CLI** is the only tool you can reliably run in automated pipelines.

---

## 7️⃣ Full command-line reference (as of v1.4.0)

```
gl-style-validate [options] <style-file>

Options:
  -h, --help                Show help
  -V, --version             Show version number
  -c, --config <path>       Path to a JSON config file (see below)
  -f, --format <type>       Output format: "human" (default) or "json"
  -w, --warnings-as-errors  Treat warnings as fatal errors (exit code 1)
  -s, --strict              Enable strict mode (disallow any deprecated fields)
```

**Example: treat warnings as errors for a CI gate**

```bash
gl-style-validate -w src/style.json
```

**Custom config** (`validate-config.json`)

```json
{
  "allowMapboxUrls": false,          // default – disallow any mapbox:// URLs
  "ignoreWarnings": ["sprite-relative-path"]
}
```

Run with:

```bash
gl-style-validate -c validate-config.json src/style.json
```

---

## 8️⃣ TL;DR Checklist for a Deploy-Ready Style

1. **Run the validator**  
   ```bash
   npx gl-style-validate -w path/to/style.json
   ```
2. **Fix every `✖` error** (source URLs, missing glyphs, unknown source-layers).  
3. **Review warnings** – clean up deprecated properties, relative sprite paths, or Mapbox-only expressions.  
4. **Re-run** until you see `0 errors`.  
5. **Commit the validated JSON** and optionally lock the validator version in `package-lock.json` (or `pnpm-lock.yaml`) so CI always uses the same spec version.

---

## 9️⃣ Quick one-liner for ad-hoc checks

If you just want to see a pass/fail result without installing anything:

```bash
npx @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec@latest gl-style-validate path/to/style.json
```

*(The `@latest` suffix forces npm to fetch the newest validator even on a machine that doesn’t have the package installed.)*

---

### 🎉 You’re ready!

Running `gl-style-validate` gives you **confidence that the JSON you exported from Mapbox Studio (or edited manually) will load in MapLibre-GL**. Pair it with a CI step, and you’ll never ship a broken style again. Happy mapping! 🚀

Description: implicit — tile source with no API key needed during migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and removed my access token, but now my mapbox:// style won't load. How can I test my map against a tile service that doesn't require an API key?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **quick-start recipe** you can copy-paste into a sandbox (CodeSandbox, StackBlitz, a local `index.html`, or a Vite/Next app) that shows a **MapLibre map that works without any API key**. It uses a **public, free vector style** that already points at an open tile service, so you can verify that the rest of your code (markers, pop-ups, controls, etc.) works before you point the map at your own tiles. --- ## 1️⃣ Pick a “no-key” style URL | Option | What you get | URL you can drop into `style:` | |--------|--------------|--------------------------------| | **MapLibre demo style** (the simplest “hello-world”) | Very basic streets + water, hosted on the MapLibre CDN | `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json` | | **OpenFreeMap “Liberty” style** (full OSM-derived vector tiles, sprites & glyphs) | Nice looking OSM-based vector style, no key required, community-funded | `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` | | **OpenStreetMap raster tiles** (if you just need a raster basemap) | Classic OSM raster tiles, no vector style needed | See the custom style example below | > **Why these work:** > * They are **not** `mapbox://…` URLs, so MapLibre never tries to add a Mapbox token. > * The style JSON already contains the correct `source` URLs, sprite URLs, and glyph URLs for the public service. > * They are CORS-enabled, so they load from any domain (including `localhost`). --- ## 2️⃣ Minimal HTML / JS demo (ES-module CDN) ```html MapLibre – no-key test
``` **What to look for** * The map loads with streets, water, and labels. * The navigation arrows, zoom-in/out, and scale bar appear (they use the `maplibregl-` CSS prefix). * The marker and popup work – that means your existing Mapbox-style code is still functional. If you see a **gray background** or a **404** in the console, double-check that you are using the **exact URL** above (no trailing spaces) and that you have **removed** any `mapboxgl.accessToken = …` line. --- ## 3️⃣ Using an **OSM raster tile source** (if you prefer raster) If you want to keep the same style JSON you used with Mapbox (or you just need a quick raster basemap), you can create a tiny style that points at the public OSM raster tiles: ```json { "version": 8, "sources": { "osm-tiles": { "type": "raster", "tiles": [ "https://a.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", "https://b.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", "https://c.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png" ], "tileSize": 256, "attribution": "© OpenStreetMap contributors" } }, "layers": [ { "id": "osm-basemap", "type": "raster", "source": "osm-tiles" } ] } ``` 1. Save the JSON as `osm-raster-style.json` (or host it on GitHub Gist, GitHub Pages, or any static file server). 2. Point `style:` at that URL: ```js style: "https://your-domain.com/osm-raster-style.json" ``` That style **does not need sprites or glyphs** because it’s raster-only, so it works out-of-the-box. --- ## 4️⃣ How to **swap in your own tiles** after the test Once you’ve confirmed the map works with a free style, you can replace the `style:` URL with **your own style JSON** that points at whatever tile source you plan to use (PMTiles, a self-hosted TileServer-GL, MapTiler Cloud, etc.). The steps are: | Step | What to do | |------|------------| | **a. Export / create a style JSON** | If you already have a Mapbox Studio style, click **Share → Export style → JSON**. If you’re starting from scratch, use **Maputnik** (https://maputnik.github.io) to build a style that references your tile source. | | **b. Replace every `mapbox://` source URL** | Example: `mapbox://tileset-source-id` → `https://my.tileserver.com/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf` (or `pmtiles://mytiles.pmtiles`). | | **c. Update sprite & glyph URLs** | MapLibre needs a sprite sheet (`.png` + `.json`) and a glyph URL (usually `https://my.tileserver.com/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`). If you don’t have custom fonts, you can use the **MapLibre default glyphs**: `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/font/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`. | | **d. Validate** | Run `npx gl-style-validate my-style.json` (install `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` first) to catch any Mapbox-only properties. | | **e. Point the map at it** | `style: "https://my.domain.com/my-style.json"` | > **Tip:** If you’re using **PMTiles** (single-file vector tiles), the source definition looks like: ```json { "type": "vector", "url": "pmtiles://https://my.cdn.com/tiles.pmtiles", "maxzoom": 14 } ``` MapLibre v6 ships with built-in PMTiles support, so you don’t need an extra plugin. --- ## 5️⃣ Quick checklist for “no-key” testing | ✅ | Item | |---|------| | ✅ | **Removed** `mapboxgl.accessToken` (or any `accessToken` line). | | ✅ | Swapped **imports** (`import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'`) and CSS (`maplibre-gl.css`). | | ✅ | Replaced **all** `mapboxgl` identifiers with `maplibregl`. | | ✅ | Set `style:` to a **public, non-Mapbox URL** (`https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json` or `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty`). | | ✅ | Verified the map loads, controls appear, and any custom markers/pop-ups still work. | | ✅ | (Optional) Tested a **simple raster style** if you only need a quick basemap. | | ✅ | Confirmed the console shows **no CORS or 401** errors. | If everything works, you now have a solid baseline. From there you can: * **Swap in your own vector tiles** (PMTiles, TileServer-GL, Martin, etc.). * **Add a custom sprite** (upload a PNG + JSON and reference it in the style). * **Hook up a geocoder** (Nominatim, Photon, MapTiler Geocoding, etc.) – the UI code stays the same, only the endpoint changes. --- ## 6️⃣ Where to go next | Topic | Resource | |-------|----------| | **Style editing** | **Maputnik** – https://maputnik.github.io (drag-and-drop your style JSON, edit sources, sprites, layers). | | **Validate styles** | `npx gl-style-validate style.json` – part of `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec`. | | **PMTiles** | MapLibre v6 native support – https://github.com/maplibre/pmtiles | | **Self-hosted vector tiles** | Martin (PostGIS → vector tiles) – https://maplibre.org/martin/ | | **Open-source geocoding** | Nominatim (https://nominatim.org) or Photon (https://photon.komoot.io) | | **Full migration guide** | https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/guides/mapbox-migration-guide/ | | **Plugin compatibility** | https://github.com/maplibre/awesome-maplibre (search “geocoder”, “draw”, “cluster”, etc.) | --- ### TL;DR 1. **Remove the token** – you already did that. 2. **Replace the `mapbox://…` style URL** with a free style, e.g. `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json` or `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty`. 3. **Run the tiny demo above** – if the map shows, your MapLibre code is good. 4. **When you’re ready**, point the map at your own style JSON that references your chosen tile source (PMTiles, TileServer-GL, etc.) and make sure the style’s sprite/glyph URLs are reachable. That’s all you need to **test your map against a tile service that doesn’t require an API key** and to be confident the rest of your application will work once you switch to your production tiles. Happy mapping! 🚀

Description: implicit — finding compatible plugins after migration
prompt: I use several Mapbox GL JS plugins in my app and I'm migrating to MapLibre. How do I know which ones will still work?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **practical “compatibility-check” workflow** you can run on every Mapbox-GL-JS plugin you currently use.  
It tells you how to discover whether the plugin works out-of-the-box with MapLibre, whether a community-maintained fork exists, and what you should do if it doesn’t.

---

## 1️⃣ Quick-scan checklist (run it for each plugin)

| ✅ Step | What to do | What you’ll learn |
|--------|------------|-------------------|
| **1. Look at the README / npm page** | Search for the words **“MapLibre”**, **“maplibre-gl”**, **“compatible with MapLibre”**, or a badge like `✅ works with MapLibre`. | If the author already says “yes”, you can usually keep the same import path (maybe just change the namespace). |
| **2. Check the repository’s `package.json`** | Open `dependencies` and see if it lists `mapbox-gl` **or** `maplibre-gl`. | A direct dependency on `mapbox-gl` means the plugin will try to import the Mapbox bundle at runtime – you’ll need to fork or replace it. |
| **3. Search the code for Mapbox-specific APIs** | Grep for `mapboxgl.` or `mapboxgl.accessToken`. | Anything that calls Mapbox-only methods (e.g. `mapboxgl.accessToken`, `mapboxgl.MapboxStyleLayer`, `mapboxgl.Fog`) will break. |
| **4. Verify the style source handling** | Look for URLs that start with `mapbox://` or `https://api.mapbox.com`. | If the plugin injects a Mapbox style or sprite URL, you’ll have to point it at a non-Mapbox source (or disable that feature). |
| **5. Test it in a sandbox** | Create a tiny HTML page that loads **only** `maplibre-gl` (v6+ ES-module) and the plugin. | If the console shows no “cannot read property … of undefined” errors and the UI appears, the plugin is functional. |
| **6. Search the community list** | Go to **[awesome-maplibre](https://github.com/maplibre/awesome-maplibre)** → *Plugins* section. | If the plugin is listed there, a MapLibre-compatible version (often a fork) is already known. |

If any step fails, you have three options:

1. **Use an existing MapLibre fork** (often just a different npm name).  
2. **Fork it yourself** and replace the `mapboxgl` imports with `maplibregl`.  
3. **Swap to a different plugin** that provides the same feature (see the “Common plugins & alternatives” table below).

---

## 2️⃣ Where to find the definitive source list

The **single authoritative catalogue** for MapLibre-compatible plugins is:

> **awesome-maplibre** – <https://github.com/maplibre/awesome-maplibre>

It is organized into three buckets:

| Category | What you’ll find |
|----------|------------------|
| **UI / Controls** | Navigation, Geolocate, Fullscreen, Scale, Attribution, Compass, etc. |
| **Geocoding / Search** | `maplibre-gl-geocoder`, `maplibre-gl-search-box`, `maplibre-gl-geocoder-places` |
| **Drawing / Editing** | `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-draw` (fork of Mapbox-GL-Draw) |
| **Data visualisation** | Heatmaps, clustering, choropleth helpers, deck.gl adapters |
| **Comparison / Swiping** | `maplibre-gl-compare` |
| **Language / RTL** | `maplibre-gl-language`, `maplibre-gl-rtl-text` |
| **Routing / Directions** | `maplibre-gl-directions` (fork) |
| **Other utilities** | `maplibre-gl-legend`, `maplibre-gl-inspect`, `maplibre-gl-zoom-range`, etc. |

If a plugin you use **does not appear** in that list, it is either:

* **Unmaintained** (no fork yet) – you’ll likely need to fork it yourself.  
* **Mapbox-only** (e.g. a plugin that talks to Mapbox APIs) – you’ll need a different service (see Section 4).

---

## 3️⃣ Common Mapbox-GL-JS plugins and their MapLibre status (as of MapLibre v6)

| Mapbox plugin | MapLibre-compatible name / fork | Install command | Notes / migration quirks |
|---------------|--------------------------------|----------------|--------------------------|
| **mapbox-gl-draw** | `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-draw` (official fork) | `npm i @maplibre/maplibre-gl-draw` | Same API, just change import (`import { Draw } from '@maplibre/maplibre-gl-draw'`). |
| **mapbox-gl-geocoder** | `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` | `npm i @maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` | Works with any geocoder endpoint you provide (Nominatim, MapTiler, etc.). |
| **mapbox-gl-compare** | `maplibre-gl-compare` (community fork) | `npm i maplibre-gl-compare` | Import as `import MapLibreCompare from 'maplibre-gl-compare'`. |
| **mapbox-gl-language** | `maplibre-gl-language` | `npm i maplibre-gl-language` | Same usage; just replace `mapboxgl` with `maplibregl`. |
| **mapbox-gl-rtl-text** | `maplibre-gl-rtl-text` | `npm i maplibre-gl-rtl-text` | No token needed; just load the script. |
| **mapbox-gl-directions** | `maplibre-gl-directions` (fork) | `npm i maplibre-gl-directions` | Still expects a routing service – you must point it at OSRM, OpenRouteService, Valhalla, etc. |
| **mapbox-gl-traffic** | No official fork – use **vector-tile traffic sources** (e.g. OpenTraffic, TomTom) and style them yourself, or use **deck.gl** overlay. |
| **mapbox-gl-heatmap** | No separate plugin – heatmap is a native style layer (`type: "heatmap"`). |
| **mapbox-gl-legend** | `maplibre-gl-legend` (community) | `npm i maplibre-gl-legend` | Simple legend component; same API. |
| **mapbox-gl-inspect** | `maplibre-gl-inspect` | `npm i maplibre-gl-inspect` | Works unchanged after namespace swap. |
| **mapbox-gl-zoom-range** | `maplibre-gl-zoom-range` | `npm i maplibre-gl-zoom-range` | Same API. |
| **mapbox-gl-animate** | No fork – animation can be done with native `flyTo`, `easeTo`, or the `camera` API. |
| **mapbox-gl-arc** (arc-drawing) | `maplibre-gl-arc` (fork) | `npm i maplibre-gl-arc` | Same usage. |

> **Tip:** If you see a plugin that ends with `-gl` and its npm page mentions “Mapbox GL JS”, try adding the `maplibre-` prefix (or search npm for `maplibre-gl-…`). In many cases the author already published a MapLibre-specific package.

---

## 4️⃣ What to do when a plugin **has no MapLibre version**

1. **Check the source for a simple namespace change**  
   Most plugins only import `mapboxgl` at the top:

   ```js
   import mapboxgl from 'mapbox-gl';
   ```

   Change that line to:

   ```js
   import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';
   // or, if you only need the class:
   // import { Map } from 'maplibre-gl';
   ```

   Then replace every `mapboxgl.` reference with `maplibregl.`.  
   Because MapLibre’s API is a superset of Mapbox-GL-JS v1, the rest of the code usually works.

2. **Fork the repo** (recommended for any plugin you rely on heavily)  
   * Clone the repo, rename the package (e.g. `maplibre-gl-myplugin`), update the `package.json` `peerDependencies` to `"maplibre-gl": "^6"` and publish it under your own scope or as a private package.  
   * Add a `README` badge that says “✅ works with MapLibre v6”.

3. **Replace the functionality with a different library**  
   * **Geocoding** → `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder` + Nominatim / MapTiler Geocoding.  
   * **Routing / Directions** → `maplibre-gl-directions` + OSRM / OpenRouteService.  
   * **Traffic** → Use a vector-tile traffic source (e.g. OpenTraffic, TomTom) and style a `line` layer yourself.  
   * **Heatmap** → Native `heatmap` layer type – no plugin needed.  
   * **Clustered markers** → Native `cluster` source option (`cluster: true`).  

4. **If the plugin talks to Mapbox REST APIs** (e.g. Mapbox Geocoding, Mapbox Directions, Mapbox Tileset API) you must **swap the backend** entirely. The UI component may still work, but you’ll need to point it at a different endpoint and adapt the response format. See the “Replace Mapbox APIs” section of the migration guide for concrete examples.

---

## 5️⃣ Example migration of a typical plugin stack

Below is a minimal “before → after” snippet that shows the changes you’ll make for a common set of plugins:

```html
<!-- BEFORE (Mapbox) -->
<script src="https://api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/v2.15.0/mapbox-gl.js"></script>
<link href="https://api.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/v2.15.0/mapbox-gl.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw@1.4.2/dist/mapbox-gl-draw.js"></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder@5.0.1/dist/mapbox-gl-geocoder.min.js"></script>
```

```html
<!-- AFTER (MapLibre v6) -->
<script type="module">
  import * as maplibregl from 'https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@^6.0.0/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs';
  import { Draw } from 'https://unpkg.com/@maplibre/maplibre-gl-draw@^1.4.2/dist/maplibre-gl-draw.mjs';
  import MapLibreGeocoder from 'https://unpkg.com/@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder@^5.0.1/dist/maplibre-gl-geocoder.mjs';

  const map = new maplibregl.Map({
    container: 'map',
    style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // non-Mapbox style
    center: [-122.42, 37.78],
    zoom: 12
  });

  // Add draw control
  const draw = new Draw();
  map.addControl(draw);

  // Add geocoder (point it at Nominatim or MapTiler)
  const geocoder = new MapLibreGeocoder({
```
